worked: Federal AGI = wages 283,250.00 = 283,250.00. Federal taxable income = 283,250.00 - 23,625.00 standard deduction = 259,625.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). RI-1040 line 1 federal AGI 283,250.00. Line 1y total decreasing modifications = 0.00. Line 2a other-state obligations 0.00; line 2m total increasing modifications = 0.00. Schedule M page 2 line 3 net = 0.00 - 0.00 = 0.00; RI-1040 line 2 = 0.00. Line 3 modified federal AGI = 283,250.00 + (0.00) = 283,250.00. Standard Deduction and Exemption Worksheets: worksheet line 5 = 283,250.00 - 254,250.00 = 29,000.00, not more than 29,000; line 6 = 29,000.00 / 7,250 = 4.0000000, a whole number 4; line 7 = 0.2000. Line 4 standard deduction: 16,350.00 (Head of household) x 0.2000 = 3,270.00. Line 5 = 283,250.00 - 3,270.00 = 279,980.00. Line 6 exemptions: 1 x 5,100.00 = 5,100.00 x 0.2000 = 1,020.00. Line 7 taxable income = 279,980.00 - 1,020.00 = 278,960.00. Line 8 tax on 278,960.00 by the schedule as numbers: 79,900.00 x 0.0375 = 2996.2500 + 101,750.00 x 0.0475 = 4833.1250 + 97,310.00 x 0.0599 = 5828.869000 = 13658.244000, 13,658.24 to the cent. Credits 0.00 (Schedule I, Schedule II, RI earned income credit and RI-1040H are not modelled and not claimed here). Rhode Island income tax = 13,658.24. Note: Exactly 29,000 over: not 'more than $29,000', so the fourth band still keeps 0.2000.
